title: Two quarter-noise weight rules worsen Kepler-90 i grid ranks with 0.5-day and 2-day filters
abstract: We test whether weights for noise in each Kepler quarter repair a failed search for known planet Kepler-90 i. We reuse fourteen release 25 light curves. At a two-day median filter, equal weights give a best nearby period rank of 4454. Residual-MAD and difference-MAD weights worsen it to 7132 and 8279. At a half-day filter, the ranks are 1650, 2004, and 1729. None of the six fixed choices selects a period match among its first 20 peaks. The supplied orbit still gives early and later depths of 83.1 and 97.7 ppm. These two weight rules do not repair this known-signal control. They do not identify the cause of other peaks or exclude new planets. Later data share the same telescope. Code, source hashes, derived results, a figure, and repeat steps are included. External observations and the orbit table stay outside the package.

display.caption: Grid ranks near the known period and early quarter noise scales. Lower rank is better. Neither quarter-weight rule repairs top-20 selection.
